prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1281; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's representative following a sideswipe that occurred while the claimant was changing lanes. The claimant reports a wrist fracture and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the driver listing and confirmed the claimant is named on the policy as a driver. Coverage was in force at the time of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, witness statements, and scene photographs. All three sources describe the claimant's vehicle as being in the adjacent lane when the other vehicle drifted over, and the other driver's account matches.

Entry 4: Inspected the vehicle. The damage pattern along the driver side is consistent with the impact described, and no prior damage in the same area appears in our records or the photos.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant's attorney. The client's account of the collision has stayed the same in every conversation so far. Medical records show a wrist fracture that is a plausible injury for this type of crash, and no earlier injury to the same area is on file.

Entry 6: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this fracture, so the file is being monitored and the treating provider's records have been requested to confirm the course of care.
